reviews.title: Most Ignorant Engineering Award
reviews.text: This is by far the most idiotic product I’ve ever seen in my life. It’s got a strap that’s designed not to move once it’s connected with the latch on the back and maybe women have mastered latching the bra from behind, but the vast majority of women that I’ve seen they just turn the bra, latch it, and then rotate it back, which polar has designed a strap intentionally that inhibits you from doing that. That’s just the idiocy displayed in usability, but then they made a product that can’t be paired with Bluetooth in accordance with the instructions that both the written and online support pages tell you to do. The described options don’t exist so you have to fiddle fumble around and in my case search outside sources to find ways to do it and I ended up having to pair using my iPhone Bluetooth manager which is specifically prohibited because it won’t allow their application to pair, but it did allow their application to see the device and then I had to forget the device on my iPhone and pair it through the application to get it to work. If these guys were building airplanes, they would have only killed half a dozen or so people before they figured out that they had built a lead balloon.

reviews.title: Polar Loop Gen 2 – The Biggest Piece of Junk I’ve Ever Owned
reviews.text:
Constant connection problems, failed syncing, and an app that often cannot detect the device even when it is right next to the phone. I’ve tried everything: reinstalling the app, restarting the phone, repairing Bluetooth, charging the device, and resetting settings, but the same issues keep coming back.

A fitness tracker should reliably track activity, not waste hours troubleshooting connection problems. The hardware and software combination is extremely frustrating and unreliable. By far the worst fitness device experience I have ever had. I would not recommend it to anyone.

reviews.title: Favorite “Activity” missing. Also, data download?
reviews.text:
I don’t post reviews in general, and negative views in particular. That said, this would be a great 5 star app if it did two additional things:
1. When I select an “Activity,” I should be able to “favorite” frequently selected activities, such as “walking” or “calisthenics” instead of having to search alphabetically amongst a too large number of activities. These favorites would show up in the menu of “favorites” that already exists. Also I should be able to dump my accumulated data, including heart rate, into spreadsheet file format download. Do those two things (or point them out time hear) and my two stars become five.

reviews.title: Polar Loop suffers from awful app
reviews.text: Coming from the Garmin world here.  Decided to take a plunge into the fitness band space and picked Polar Loop due to screenless device, design, and polar’s reputation in sensor tech.  While I do overall like the app and appreciate it’s daily wear and comfort over the very large Garmin watches, the app really is as bad as could be.  I am willing to be somewhat patient to see how the new updates coming in phase 3 land (2026?).  But if Garmin comes out with a similar style band this year I will happily go back due to the app alone.  Not interested in paying a monthly subscription for my data and app access so that leaves mostly Polar and Garmin as my options.  Polar has the hardware advantage for now, but they are nowhere remotely close Garmin’s app features, capabilities and reporting.

reviews.title: Poor Update
reviews.text:
Since the latest update to the UI, it might be “cleaner” but it’s not as helpful as now I find myself having to go into each section instead of getting a good glance in my diary, if I wanted to go into each section before I could, but feel it’s more of a necessity now. 
Also the latest firmware just sometimes does not want to bring over any sleep data, I sometimes need to sync Polar Flow twice, sometimes the data never comes over. This is a shame because when I started using everything in November it was great.
